headline: High: Claude Code can write shared files and n8n can execute server-side commands, creating dangerous default pathways for prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading automation errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code shares state via filesystem and git, and n8n can read/write server files and orchestrate workflows. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from Claude Code can be consumed by n8n as trusted workflow input. The pathway is not fully automatic, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes untrusted content into a file or git state that n8n later ingests as workflow input, injection is possible.
IF n8n parses Claude Code output as instructions without provenance checks, prompt injection can propagate.
mitigations: Use separate directories and repos for the two agents.
Add a manual review step before n8n consumes Claude Code output.
Require provenance tags on files passed between agents.
Disable automatic ingestion of free-form text into n8n workflows.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and can send data through many integrations. If the pair shares files or workflow inputs, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Claude Code into n8n and then out through connected systems. The blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Claude Code places secrets or source code into files that n8n reads, leakage can occur.
IF an n8n workflow forwards those files to an external integration node, exfiltration occurs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared working directories.
Restrict n8n workflows to non-sensitive paths.
Turn off or gate external integration nodes for shared inputs.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Review file contents before any n8n upload step.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shell commands. Claude Code also modifies git state, while n8n can run Execute Command on the server. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state or overwrite each other. Because the overlap is on mutable resources with no stated locking, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF n8n Execute Command and Claude Code modify the same git branch without locks, repository state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable git writes from one agent during the other's run.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestrator that can act on workflow outputs, and Claude Code can generate code, shell commands, or file edits that n8n may treat as authoritative. Without an explicit verification step, Claude Code errors can cascade into n8n actions such as command execution or integration calls. That default automation path makes high severity appropriate.
conditions: IF n8n uses Claude Code output as a workflow variable or command payload, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF the workflow lacks validation before Execute Command or integration nodes, errors cascade.
mitigations: Insert a validation node before any action node.
Require human approval for command execution.
Constrain Claude Code output to structured schemas.
Log and diff outputs before execution.
Disable auto-run on newly generated workflow steps.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code runs on the invoking user’s host and handles local source code and git history, while n8n stores workflow data on its server and can route it through connected systems. If regulated data is placed into shared workflows, retention and residency can diverge between the two systems. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents, their logging and retention settings must match.
IF n8n stores workflow artifacts longer than the host-side Claude Code session, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs.
Document data residency for each integration node.
Use redacted test data for cross-agent workflows.
